column1: # Shared CONNECT-authority grammar for the desktop (Rust) and Android (Kotlin)
# Consumers (both load THIS file, neither keeps its own copy of the vectors):
#       connect authority vectors agree with the rust parser (test resource)
# Format: tab-separated, one vector per line, '#' starts a comment, blank lines
# `accept` means the PARSER accepts the authority-form (RFC 3986 §3.2.3,
# `host ":" port`). It does NOT mean the destination is allowed: `127.0.0.1:443`
# parses and is then refused by the address policy, exactly like an ordinary
# page requesting loopback. `reject` means the request line is refused before
# any lookup, socket or policy decision.
# Why a shared file: until round 22 the desktop parser accepted three forms
# Android refuses — a signed port (`+443`, because `u16::from_str` accepts it),
# a bracketed IPv4 (`[8.8.8.8]:443`), and an unbracketed `a:b` host — so "is
# this request tunnelled" depended on the platform. The vectors below are the
# grammar both parsers must implement; adding a form to one parser alone now
# Not covered here (documented in docs/security-residual-risks.md): the request
# line itself (method, HTTP version, header framing) and the destination policy.
